Introductory statement: This position is assigned to the Force Support Squadron (FSS) Resource Management Office and reports directly to the Resource Management Flight Chief.

The primary purpose of this position is to manage the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Accounting Office for the Buckley Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR), Lodging Funds, and assigned Geographically Separated Unit (GSU) MWR Funds.

Duties and Responsibilities: Serves as the subject matter expert (SME) with independent responsibility for all accounting aspects of the Buckley MWR, Lodging, and assigned GSU MWR Funds, ensuring the overall integrity, accuracy, and propriety of the NAF accounting system, including all financial records, reports, and statements.

Provides comprehensive technical and administrative supervision over subordinate staff, including accounting technicians, clerks, and cashiers-by planning, organizing, directing, and evaluating program activities, determining work distribution, setting and adjusting priorities, and conducting informal training and cross-training to build back-up capabilities.

Executes a full range of supervisory personnel management duties, to include the selection, promotion, reassignment, and discipline of personnel, while establishing clear work requirements, timelines, and expected results both verbally and in writing.

Supervises staff performance across a full range of accounting duties using double-entry accrual methods for income and expense reporting, accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, inventory, and general ledger operations.

Monitors and approves financial transactions, operating statements, and subsidiary account tracking prepared by subordinates, and utilizes experienced judgment and research to resolve complex, non-standard transactions and out-of-balance conditions.

Oversees the Cash Management Investment Program (CMIP) to ensure deposits and distributions are balanced daily, enforces strict internal controls and separation of duties for overall funds integrity, and ensures management is kept aware of unusual financial variances or program changes.

Communicates directly with higher headquarters regarding accounting procedures and banking transactions, participates in financial management meetings with key stakeholders, and maintains the Life of the Fund file for each assigned fund.

Additionally, approves routine requests for Unit Funds and Special Morale & Welfare (SM&W) Funds, acts as the alternate Installation Program Coordinator for the NAF Purchase Card Program, maintains a contract warrant to serve as the alternate NAF Contracting Officer, and performs other related duties as assigned.

PERFORMANCE STANDARDS Performs all assigned duties in an accurate and timely manner, working independently to establish a work schedule based on operational requirements and deadlines. Responds to and communicates with both internal and external customers promptly and courteously.

Accurately maintains and updates all files to enable quick, efficient retrieval of information and ensure strict compliance with established directives. Ensures the overall integrity and accountability of systems maintained, actively guarding against system compromise.

Conducts effective problem-solving regarding the assigned mission with minimal supervision and ensures that all accounts and subsidiary ledgers in the assigned area are properly maintained and reconciled to produce accurate financial statements by established due dates.

We’re looking for an experienced, full-time Executive Assistant to join our team in Berlin and support our Co-CEOs, Lennard and Judith.
In this role, you’ll work closely with our Co-CEOs, Lennard and Judith, as part of a young, entrepreneurial team. If you thrive in fast-paced environments, love bringing order to hectic schedules, and approach each day with a proactive mindset, we’d love to meet you.
We’re looking for someone highly organized, calm, self-motivated, and adaptable.

Internal organisation and steering. You run the CEO's operating rhythm. Calendar, inbox triage, meeting preparation, and follow-through all sit with you. You keep an eye on details and you keep the leadership cadence (weeklies, board preparation, offsites) moving.
External travel and speaking. You plan and book complex international travel end to end, and you manage the speaking pipeline: inbound requests, selection, briefing packs, and logistics on the ground.
C-level relationship management. You become the trusted point of contact for the CEO's most important external relationships: customers, partners, and investors. You track who needs a touchpoint and when, and protect these relationships through reliability and proactivity.
Augmentation and anticipation. You work half a step ahead of everyone else in the room. You can identify a bottleneck before it forms. You build the systems, defaults and briefings that let the CEO spend their time on judgement rather than logistics.
Admin. You manage expenses and finance admin and can support with occasional personal assistant (PA) duties as needed.
CEO office collaboration. You’ll work in very close coordination with the CEO office, which includes a Chief of Staff and CEO Office Manager who are responsible for operational processes in the CEO office. Incl. performance management, KPI tracking, leadership accountability and strategic projects.
You Might Be a Fit If…
You have previously supported a CEO or equivalent in a demanding organisation and are looking for another environment that gives you an opportunity to grow.
You want to be in a young, fast company. You are comfortable with ambiguity, short timelines and a team that is still writing its own playbook, and you would rather shape the system than inherit a finished one.
You are mission-driven. You care that European companies build and adopt AI, and you want your work to count toward that rather than toward a job title. You are eager to automate your own work where possible.
AI can do a lot of things, but in the short term, it won't be able to shepherd a growing group of mostly young people in a very dynamic environment. We are looking for someone who can foster the most important human qualities within the organization.
We are looking for a long-term partner, not someone optimizing for their next role.
Personified calmness – You bring order, not chaos. When things get hectic, you're the person who slows down, thinks clearly, and helps others do the same. Your presence makes people feel like things are under control. You instill calmness and continuity in the organization.
Good judgment – You know what matters and what doesn't. You read people well. You understand when to push and when to give space, when something is urgent and when it can wait.
Compassionate and empathetic – You care about the people around you. You understand that behind every missed deadline or dropped ball is a human with hidden context. You hold people accountable with kindness.
Ownership mentality – You see problems and fix them without being asked. You don't wait for permission. You follow through.
Strong communicator – Written and verbal. You can draft important emails or have a difficult conversation with equal skill.
Trustworthy – You'll have access to everything and work directly with the CEO. Discretion and trust are very important.
You are a kind person who cares about the people around you.
The Environment
We work from our office in Berlin, Greifswalder Strasse 212. Everyone works together in person because the hardest problems get solved faster at a whiteboard than in a Slack thread. Conversations happen faster, problems get solved quicker, and we actually know each other.
Days start at 8:30. Lunch & dinner are together. We run, go to the gym, and take care of ourselves. Health is not separate from work here, it is part of how we work well.
The vibe is calm but intense. No one is yelling or panicking. But everyone is working hard on things that matter.

We will figure out the right level together based on your experience and scope. Levels are about the work you own, not your title or years of experience. We narrow down the expected salary range early in the process.

## À propos du Département des Affaires étrangères et du Commerce ##
Le rôle du Département des Affaires étrangères et du Commerce (DFAT) est de promouvoir les intérêts de l'Australie et des Australiens à l'international.

Cela implique de renforcer la sécurité de l'Australie, d'améliorer sa prospérité, de fournir un programme d'aide étrangère efficace et de haute qualité, et d'aider les voyageurs australiens ainsi que les Australiens à l'étranger. Le département fournit des conseils en politique étrangère, commerciale et de développement au gouvernement australien.

Le DFAT collabore également avec d'autres agences gouvernementales australiennes pour coordonner la poursuite des intérêts globaux, régionaux et bilatéraux de l'Australie.
## À propos du poste ##
Sous la direction, l'Assistant Exécutif de l'Ambassadeur et du Vice-Ambassadeur fournit un soutien exécutif, administratif et organisationnel de haut niveau à la Mission Permanente d'Australie auprès des Nations Unies à Genève. Le poste organise également des événements et fonctions officiels.
En raison de la nature sensible du travail, ce poste nécessite de pouvoir obtenir et maintenir une habilitation de sécurité nationale reconnue par le DFAT.
## Les principales responsabilités du poste incluent, sans s'y limiter : ##
* Fournir un soutien exécutif de haut niveau à l'Ambassadeur et au Vice-Ambassadeur, assurant le bon fonctionnement des bureaux exécutifs dans un environnement rapide et sensible.
* Gérer et prioriser la correspondance, les invitations, les documents d'information et les demandes, en faisant preuve d'un jugement avisé pour déterminer les priorités, les actions et les exigences de conformité.
* Coordonner les visites officielles et les programmes de délégation pour les ministres, hauts fonctionnaires et visiteurs de haut niveau, en équilibrant les priorités concurrentes et les exigences opérationnelles.
* Planifier et organiser des événements de représentation, des réunions et des engagements officiels, en liaison avec les parties prenantes internes et externes pour atteindre les objectifs de la Mission.
* Gérer les dépenses de représentation et l'administration financière, y compris les prévisions, les justifications, les rapprochements et les rapports conformément aux politiques et procédures du DFAT.
* Coordonner les déplacements, la logistique et les arrangements administratifs liés aux activités de la direction exécutive et officielles, en assurant la conformité aux politiques et procédures pertinentes.
* Surveiller les risques liés à la sécurité, aux opérations et au flux de travail, en mettant en œuvre les contrôles nécessaires et en escaladant les problèmes le cas échéant.
* Fournir des conseils administratifs, maintenir des systèmes d'affaires efficaces et soutenir la coordination de l'équipe, contribuant à l'amélioration continue et à l'efficacité organisationnelle.
## Qualifications/Expérience/Connaissances/Compétences requises ##
* Expérience avérée dans un rôle similaire d'Assistant Exécutif
* Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale
* Capacité à travailler en équipe et à soutenir celle-ci. Capacité à développer et maintenir des relations respectueuses et efficaces avec les parties prenantes internes et externes
* Capacité à gérer le temps, à prioriser, planifier, gérer plusieurs tâches et travailler efficacement sous pression
* Compétences en gestion financière et organisationnelle
* Discrétion et jugement avisé dans la gestion d'informations confidentielles
* Expérience étendue de l'utilisation de Microsoft Office et des applications électroniques
* Compétences exceptionnelles en service client et en relations interpersonnelles
* Maîtrise de l'anglais requise, la maîtrise du français étant fortement appréciée
* Connaissance ou capacité à acquérir rapidement une connaissance de la législation du gouvernement australien ou des politiques et directives départementales relatives aux fonctions du poste
## Souhaitable ##
* Expérience préalable dans une ambassade, une organisation internationale ou un environnement comparable.
## Exigences de sécurité ##
* Habilitation de sécurité NV2 australienne ou capacité à l'obtenir et la maintenir. Les candidats doivent donc être citoyens australiens pour être considérés.
* Veuillez noter que les candidats détenant la citoyenneté ou la double citoyenneté suisse ne sont pas éligibles à une habilitation de sécurité australienne.

In addition, the EAUSA may be given primary responsibility for cases in either the Civil or Criminal Divisions.

Responsibilities will increase and assignments will become more complex as your training and experience progress. Security Requirements: Initial appointment is conditioned upon a satisfactory preemployment adjudication. This includes fingerprint, credit and tax checks, and drug testing.

In addition, continued employment is subject to a favorable adjudication of a background investigation. Residency Requirements: Assistant United States Attorneys generally must reside in the district to which he or she is appointed or within 25 miles thereof. See 28 U.S.C. 545 for district-specific information.

Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law. See www.sss.gov.
Required Qualifications: Applicants must possess a J.D. Degree and be an active member of the bar (any U.S. jurisdiction). United States citizenship is required. Preferred Qualifications: Preferred applicant must exhibit the ability to work in a supportive and professional manner with other attorneys, support staff, and client agencies.

Thus, the ideal candidate has a positive history of working collaboratively both with colleagues, and with various interested parties. These would include community groups, victims, witnesses, client entities, courts, bar associations and law enforcement entities.

Assigning and monitoring Program Support Assistant (PSA)'s work assignments to ensure a balanced distribution and flow of work. Conducting PSA staff meetings to share information, discuss case process and administrative problems, and exchange ideas.

Utilizing office automation systems to prepare in final form a variety of letters, narrative reports, memos, and other textual documents.
All qualifications and eligibility requirements must be met by the closing date of the announcement. IDEAL CANDIDATE STATEMENT The Ideal Candidate for the Office Manager position has experience maintaining the operational controls and efficiencies of an office.

The candidate has experience providing senior level administrative support to a senior manager/supervisor and can form interpersonal relationships within organizational units. The ideal candidate has exemplary communication skills and can survey operations to ensure the effectiveness of processes.

Good judgement, meticulous attention to detail, and the ability to understand of policies, procedures, and practices of a highly functional office is essential.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Applicants must have one year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level, which has provided them with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the Office Manager at the GS-09 grade level.

Specialized experience includes: Experience planning and providing management and program services to promote the operational activities of an office; and Experience providing case management assistance to managers and/or legal professionals; and Experience using spreadsheets, flowcharts and other data systems to assist in the management of funds.

OR EDUCATION: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or two (2) full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related.

Please do not cut and paste the specialized experience from this announcement into your resume, as this will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position.

TIME-IN-GRADE REQUIREMENTS All agency employees must meet time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year of experience at the GS-07 or equivalent grade level of the federal service, is required to qualify for this position.

We are hiring an Executive Assistant to the Founders to own the calendars, correspondence, travel, and follow-through of our two co-founders.
Pairs is where founders come to raise capital. We pair them with the right investors from a large, engaged global investor network, then our agents manage the relationships that turn into meetings. It is a two-sided platform, live with paying clients, profitable and self-funded, built by a small, senior, flat team that ships fast.

The two co-founders carry the work that decides this company: product, clients, the investor network, the brand. Their time is the scarcest resource in the business, and protecting it will be your mandate.

You manage both calendars across time zones, own both inboxes, plan and oversee travel, prepare the founders for the meetings that matter, and ensure every commitment they make is kept. This is a position of ownership, not a list of tasks.

You exercise judgment, act independently, and involve the founders only when a decision genuinely requires them. You work AI-first, like the rest of the company: tooling carries the mechanical work, and your time goes to judgment, anticipation, and trust.

You report directly to both co-founders and hold one of the most trusted positions in the company.
What you will own
Both calendars across time zones: scheduling, conflicts resolved before they surface, preparation time protected, and our Monday and Thursday meeting rhythm maintained.
Both inboxes: triaged daily, replies drafted in each founder's voice, nothing important left waiting.
Travel end to end: planned, booked, briefed, and resolved in real time when plans change.
Meeting preparation and follow-through: the right briefing beforehand, actions captured and pursued afterward.
The commitment layer: what the founders have promised, to whom, by when, tracked to completion.
The systems behind it all, built on the best AI tooling, so mechanical work never requires attention twice.

Have owned travel end to end, including disruptions resolved before the principal ever felt them.
Can support two principals at once: competing priorities held, both agendas moving, neither founder resolving minor conflicts.
Treat discretion as a reflex: names, transactions, and conversations remain confidential, always.

Direct trust from both co-founders, full visibility into the company, and a position that grows as the company does.

Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy.

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

This is not a traditional EA role. The Senior Executive Assistant II to our VP of Customer Success operates as a trusted extension of executive leadership — equal parts strategic operator, project manager, and thought partner. You will sit at the center of a large, fast-moving organization and use your judgment, initiative, and influence to keep the VP and his team running at peak velocity.
You will own the executive experience end-to-end: anticipating needs before they're voiced, navigating complex stakeholder dynamics, and turning ambiguous requests into crisp execution. If you thrive in environments where no two days are the same and you find energy in being the connective tissue of a high-performing org, this role is for you.
This is a remote role based in the US, however candidates must be able to support west coast hours and be open to travel 1 trip per month. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.
You Should Apply If
You want to work on problems that matter. Samsara connects the physical and digital worlds — keeping workers safe, supply chains moving, and emissions in check. Your leverage as an EBP is real.
You're an operator, not just a coordinator. You see the system behind every calendar invite, build processes that outlast you, and default to ownership over escalation.
You thrive with ambiguity and pace. You can hold ten priorities, drop the right three, and communicate clearly about all of it — without being asked twice.
You care about the craft. Being a truly elite EBP is a skill. You're always learning, always refining, and you take pride in raising the bar for everyone around you.
What You'll Own
Executive presence & flow — Manage the VP's calendar, communications, and daily operating rhythm with a level of foresight that makes him feel three steps ahead.
Complex travel & logistics — Plan and book multi-leg domestic and international travel (~1 trip/month), anticipating buffers, prep materials, and regional stakeholder touchpoints before they're requested.
Stakeholder management — Act as a trusted liaison to senior leaders, investors, and cross-functional partners internally and externally; you represent leaders in every interaction.
Operational continuity — Own expenses, team meeting agendas, action item tracking, and the behind-the-scenes coordination that keeps a large org accountable and moving.
